title: PolicyAcceptanceRecord
description: An explicit human decision to accept, or refuse to accept, specific failing findings under a specific policy version. Immutable once written. This record is the ONLY thing that can make a blocking finding non-blocking for delivery — and it does so without touching the finding: the validator's FAIL stays FAIL, in the evidence and in the UI, for the life of the mission. A delivery covered by one of these is 'delivered with an accepted exception', never 'compliant' and never 'passed'.

decision.description: REJECT is recorded so a refusal is auditable. It has no routing consequence: the finding simply stays blocking.

accepted_by.description: Verified user id, taken from the server session. Never read from the request body — a caller who could name the approver could forge an approval.

organization_id.description: Tenant that made the decision. An acceptance is refused for a mission in a different organization.

finding_refs.description: Exactly which findings this covers. A blanket acceptance is not representable: there is no wildcard.

reason.description: Written human rationale. The minimum length is real: 'ok' is not a rationale, and an acceptance nobody can justify later is one nobody should be able to make now.

expires_at.description: Optional review date. Null means no expiry — permitted, but the UI shows it as such rather than leaving it blank.

baseline_ref.description: The policy version this decision was made under. A resealed profile has a different hash, so every prior acceptance stops matching — a decision made under one policy is not a decision under another, and there is deliberately no carry-forward.

audit.description: What was on screen when the person decided.

evidence_digest.description: sha256 of the evidence set the decision was made against. This is how STALE STATE is detected: if validators have re-run and the findings changed, the digest no longer matches and the acceptance does not apply to what is on screen now.
